zuspin roadmap

Goal: vendor libspin, the library form of the Spin model checker, into an R package that installs from source on Linux, macOS and Windows with R’s own toolchain, and expose parsing, verifier generation, LTL translation and simulation to R.

The C-side work (removing exit(), redirecting output, resetting globals) is libspin’s roadmap, not this one. Stages here depend on libspin stages as noted; do not start a stage whose dependency is not tagged.

What we are vendoring

Property Value Consequence for us
License BSD 3-Clause Compatible with MIT; LICENSE.note names Spin’s copyright, authors as cph/ctb
Language C99, no external dependencies No configure, no SystemRequirements; the lowest-risk vendoring in the family
Parser yacc grammar; libspin commits the bison output Vendor the generated y.tab.c, never run bison at install
Build plain make, object list from libspin’s tools/objects.sh src/Makevars lists objects explicitly, generated by our vendor script
Output callbacks (libspin Stage 2) The shim writes to Rprintf/REprintf, or captures into a character vector
Files pan.* under a workdir Always a fresh tempfile() directory unless the user passes one
Preprocessing not in the library Done from R with the C compiler R was built with (Stage 4), or skipped
Threading one instance at a time, sequential calls Matches R; a single context lives for the package’s lifetime

Stage 0 — Package identity and API decision

  • Fill DESCRIPTION: Title, Description, Authors@R (Gerard J. Holzmann as cph, ctb), SystemRequirements: C99 is not needed; add URL/BugReports.
  • Public R API, smallest first:
    • spin_parse(path, ...) → diagnostics and symbol table as a tibble-free data frame
    • spin_generate(path, dir = tempfile(), separate = NULL) → paths of pan.*
    • spin_ltl(formula, name = NULL) → never claim as a character string
    • spin_simulate(path, seed = NULL, max_steps = NULL, trail = NULL) → captured output as lines, plus the exit status
    • spin_verify() (Stage 5) → generate, compile with R’s C compiler, run pan, parse the report
  • No preprocessing in Stage 0–3: #include/#define in a model is an error with a clear message until Stage 4.

Exit: DESCRIPTION is real; this list is copied into CLAUDE.md as the contract.

Stage 1 — Toolchain spike (no Spin yet) — depends on nothing

Prove the shape before importing 26k lines: a src/ with one vendored-style C file compiled from an explicit object list, an init.c with R_registerRoutines, and a spin_toolchain() that reports the compiler and __STDC_VERSION__. Run the full CI matrix including Windows and the r-devel containers. This is cheap for C99, and it establishes the Makevars conventions: portable make, hand-listed objects, no Makevars.win, -D__USE_MINGW_ANSI_STDIO=1.

Exit: green matrix on an empty shell.

Stage 2 — Vendor libspin — depends on libspin v0.1.0 (its Stage 4)

  • tools/vendor.sh: clone the pinned tag, copy Src/ (library objects only, no CLI) to src/libspin/, copy include/spin.h, record version/commit/date and per-file checksums in tools/vendor/, regenerate the object list in src/Makevars from libspin’s tools/objects.sh. Idempotent: delete and rebuild, git status must be clean on re-run.
  • tools/vendor/verify and a vendor.yml workflow that fail when the vendored tree differs from upstream-at-tag plus our patches.
  • Patches, if any, live in tools/patches/ and are reapplied by the script. Expected to be empty: anything R needs should be a libspin feature, not a zuspin patch.
  • LICENSE.note, inst/COPYRIGHTS if R CMD check asks.

Exit: R CMD INSTALL builds the whole library into zuspin.so; spin_version() returns libspin’s string.

Stage 3 — The shim — depends on Stage 2

  • src/shim.c: one static spin_ctx * created at load (R_init_zuspin), destroyed at unload. Sinks write through Rprintf/REprintf, or into a growable buffer when the R call asked for capture.
  • Error firewall: every .Call runs the libspin action, then cleans up, then raises with Rf_error from a message copied out of the context. Nothing may Rf_error while a libspin frame is on the stack; the arena would survive the longjmp.
  • Interrupts: pass an interrupt callback (libspin Stage 5) that checks R_CheckUserInterrupt without letting it jump, via R_ToplevelExec; return non-zero so libspin unwinds through spin_bail().
  • Strings crossing the boundary are declared UTF-8: Rf_translateCharUTF8() in, Rf_mkCharCE(…, CE_UTF8) out. Promela identifiers are ASCII, but printf strings and file paths are not guaranteed to be.
  • spin_parse, spin_generate, spin_ltl, spin_simulate as above, with testthat tests over a handful of Examples/*.pml copied into inst/extdata/ (license allows it).

Exit: the four functions work on macOS, Linux and Windows CI; a test calls each twice and compares results.

Stage 4 — Preprocessing from R — depends on Stage 3

  • spin_preprocess(path, defines = character()) runs the C preprocessor R was configured with (R CMD config CC plus -E -x c), via processx/system2, into a temp file that the library then reads. On Windows this is Rtools’ gcc, which every user installing from source already has.
  • preprocess = TRUE default on the four functions; FALSE is the fast path.

Exit: models with #include and #define work; the preprocessor command is visible in a verbose option for debugging.

Stage 5 — Verification workflow — depends on Stage 4

  • spin_verify(path, dir, options = spin_pan_options(...)): generate pan.c, compile with the same compiler as Stage 4 and the -D flags from the options (SAFETY, BITSTATE, COLLAPSE, NP, …), run ./pan with runtime flags, capture and parse the report (errors, states, memory, depth) into a list, and keep the trail file when there is one.
  • spin_trail(path, trail) replays through spin_simulate(trail = ).
  • This stage is pure R plus processx; nothing in C. Cross-platform differences are in executable suffix and quoting.

Exit: spin_verify() on peterson.pml reports no errors; on a model with a deliberate assertion violation it returns the trail and spin_trail() shows the counterexample.

Stage 6 — Hardening — depends on Stage 3

ASan/UBSan builds in CI (R CMD INSTALL --configure-args is not available, so use ~/.R/Makevars on the sanitizer leg), valgrind on Linux, gctorture(TRUE) through the test suite, rchk container, covr. Repeated calls in one session, failure followed by success, interrupts in a long simulation, UTF-8 paths.

Stage 7 — Documentation

README with a worked verify-and-replay example, a vignette on Promela from R, pkgdown reference grouped by parse/generate/verify/simulate, NEWS.md. State plainly that the library is sequential, not concurrent.

Stage 8 — CRAN

cran-extrachecks, cran-comments.md, spell check, URL check, the inst/COPYRIGHTS question, no writing outside tempdir() in examples or tests.

Deferred, decided

  • In-process pan. pan.c is a program with its own globals and exit() calls; running it in-process would mean doing to it everything libspin did to Spin. Out of scope.
  • A term/AST API over Spin’s Lextok. Interesting, but the AST is mutated by generation and has no stable upstream contract. Not before 1.0.
